comment: The multipliers and divisors are module state rather than parameters (Hammer.cpp:75), so they are not reset or randomized by Rack's own commands but by the module's own handlers, which set every ratio to one on a reset and draw a multiplier of 0 to 12 and a divisor of 1 to 9 on a randomize (Hammer.cpp:236). Each channel reads the ratio at its rotated position (Hammer.cpp:527), so a button at one row can be driving another row's output once ROTATE is turned. A channel whose multiplier is 0 holds its output at 0V (Hammer.cpp:566).
